methodological_rigor.justification: Preclinical study combining in vitro bladder cancer cell assays (RT-112, T24, SCaBER) with the in ovo TUM-CAM model. Uses IC25-based dose-finding, coefficient of drug interaction (CDI) for synergy, long-term live-cell imaging for kinetics, and ROS profiling with NAC/catalase scavenger controls to establish mechanism. Reasonable experimental design with complementary assays. Weaknesses include: mechanistic ROS scavenging only performed in SCaBER (one of three cell lines), no sample-size justification, replicate numbers not explicitly stated in main text, TUM-CAM model has single-dose/schedule and intra-group variability prevented statistical significance for tumor weight/vessel density. Statistical methods listed (t-test, ANOVA, nonlinear regression) are appropriate but no multiplicity correction for the many cytokine comparisons across three cell lines; Principal component analysis used descriptively. Significance threshold notation has a minor error ('p > 0.05 (ns)').

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical mechanistic and pharmacodynamic study (Oxford LoE 5). The therapeutic concept (plasma-cisplatin combination to enable cisplatin dose reduction in bladder cancer) has plausible clinical relevance given cisplatin toxicity limits, and the authors appropriately cite early clinical plasma trials for bladder cancer delivery via urethrocystoscopy. However, the translational gap is substantial: single-dose in vitro and CAM experiments, no immune-competent in vivo model, and technical challenges of uniform urothelial plasma exposure acknowledged. Translational path is plausible but early.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is the relevant standard for the in ovo animal-surrogate work; the manuscript describes the TUM-CAM protocol, egg source, incubation conditions, and treatment parameters with reasonable detail. kINPen plasma device specifications, flow rates, and distance are explicit. However, ARRIVE is not explicitly cited; replicate numbers, randomization, and blinding details for flow cytometry and cytokine analyses are not clearly described; supplementary and figure data are referenced without full in-text numerical results. No data or code availability statement; no sample-size justification. Cytokine multiplex panel (13 analytes) is reported without adjustment for multiple testing.

novelty_literature.justification: Cold plasma-chemotherapy combinations in cancer have precedent including prior bladder cancer work by the same group (Gelbrich 2022, cited as ref 19) and plasma-cisplatin combinations in HNSCC (Brunner 2022) and Ewing sarcoma (Nitsch 2023). Novel contributions include: systematic CDI-based synergy/additivity mapping across three histologically distinct bladder cancer lines, identification of H2O2 as a major mediator in SCaBER, and the translational comparison between in vitro synergy and TUM-CAM modest effects. Meaningful incremental extension of an established field rather than a first-in-class finding.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized and clearly written with logical progression from monotherapy dose-finding, to combination synergy analysis, to mechanistic ROS work, to in ovo validation. Discussion is substantive, contextualizing findings against prior bladder and other-tumor plasma literature and addressing the discrepancy between in vitro synergy and in ovo modest effects with biologically plausible explanations (tumor architecture, single-dose scheduling). Figures (including PCA, marker analyses, cytokine panels) are extensively referenced. Language is generally fluent with occasional verbose passages.

key_strengths: Systematic three-cell-line analysis (urothelial RT-112, T24, and squamous SCaBER) with CDI-based synergy quantification and kinetic live-cell imaging
Mechanistic ROS profiling in SCaBER identifying H2O2 as a major contributor, with appropriate NAC and catalase scavenger controls
Integration of in vitro results with the TUM-CAM in ovo model including tumor mass, vascularization, flow cytometric DAMP/EMT markers, and multiplex cytokine panel
Candid acknowledgment of the gap between in vitro synergy and in ovo modest effects, with biologically plausible explanations and explicit translational caveats
Use of a clinically approved plasma device (kINPen) and reference to first-in-human bladder plasma trial
key_concerns: Mechanistic ROS scavenger experiments performed in only one of three cell lines (SCaBER), limiting generalizability of H2O2 claim
Replicate numbers, randomization, and blinding for flow cytometry, cytokine panels, and CAM endpoints not clearly reported; no sample-size justification
No multiplicity correction for 13-cytokine multiplex across three cell lines and multiple treatment arms, raising false-discovery risk
Single-dose, single-schedule TUM-CAM treatments produced nonsignificant tumor-weight and vessel-density differences; dose-/schedule-finding in ovo not performed
No data or code sharing; ARRIVE checklist not explicitly followed
Clinical translatability for intravesical plasma delivery remains technically open despite early trial cited
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically sound preclinical study of plasma-cisplatin combinations in bladder cancer with complementary in vitro and TUM-CAM evaluation; incremental novelty and reporting gaps place it at Tier 3 with minor revisions.
